answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 53% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and therefore nobody profits from it. Because the meadow forfeiture is applied at exit, the velvet ledger totals each burn, and the sonnet audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 48 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
